title: Microscopic origin of the chiral pressure in a two-dimensional fluid
abstract: We show that a two-dimensional chiral fluid supports an antisymmetric contribution to the pressure, and determine its microscopic expression. Its origin lies outside the standard kinetic and collisional channels of the normal pressure tensor, stemming instead from the average of a parity-breaking pseudo-scalar. This chiral pressure is set by the rotational (vortex) viscosity of micropolar hydrodynamics, whose kinetic value for rough disks we compute here, to Gaussian order. Crucially, both the chiral pressure and the rotational viscosity survive at zeroth order in the gradients, meaning they persist even in the fully homogeneous fluid -- which we show is not only well defined but steady (the Quiescent Chiral State, QCS). Since this averaged pseudo-scalar does not vanish in a chiral fluid, any expansion of its distribution function must contain terms in this pseudo-scalar variable.
summary: This work derives the microscopic origin of the chiral pressure in a 2D chiral fluid, showing it arises from an orbital moment related to the particle's spin mismatch with the local flow. The chiral pressure is found to be non-zero even in a steady, homogeneous state, demonstrating a fundamental, non-dissipative mechanical response to chirality.
main_problem: The paper determines the microscopic origin and mathematical expression for the antisymmetric contribution to the pressure, known as the chiral pressure ($p_R$), in a two-dimensional chiral fluid.
main_result: The chiral pressure is proportional to the orbital moment ($\ell_O$), which quantifies the mismatch between the mean spin ($\Omega$) and half the local vorticity ($\omega/2$). This pressure persists even in a homogeneous, steady state (QCS).
method: The derivation uses a combination of hydrodynamic comparisons (cell-scale vs. particle-scale) and microscopic kinematics, analyzing the spin balance equation to derive the constitutive relations.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional fluid composed of rough, actively rotating particles (disks). The analysis treats the fluid dynamics using concepts from micropolar hydrodynamics.
key_observables: Chiral pressure ($p_R$), Orbital moment ($\ell_O$), Rotational viscosity ($\mu_R$), Quiescent Chiral State (QCS).
important_parameters: The chiral pressure and viscosity are computed to Gaussian order in gradients, and the system depends on particle properties like moment of inertia ($mI$) and collision parameters ($ eta, \kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes structural asymmetry causing parity breaking and is accurate to second order in gradients, neglecting higher-order translational-rotational correlations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the hydrodynamic derivation of the orbital moment ($\ell_O$) at different scales. Figure 2 shows the microscopic derivation relating particle spin, flow, and peculiar velocity. Figure 3 details the dependence of rotational viscosity ($\mu_R$) on restitution and inertia.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for $p_R$ by analyzing the spin balance equation. It then derives $\ell_O$ using both coarse-graining and microscopic kinematics. Finally, it computes the constitutive relation for $p_R$ and $\mu_R$, showing their persistence in the QCS.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics, the concept of persistent, non-equilibrium stress (chiral pressure) arising from intrinsic particle asymmetry is analogous to emergent topological or chiral responses studied in quantum many-body systems.
